title: 2019 AMC 10B Problem 9
statement: The function \(f\) is defined by \[f(x) = \lfloor|x|\rfloor - |\lfloor x \rfloor|\] for all real numbers \(x,\) where \(\lfloor r \rfloor\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to the real number \(r.\) What is the range of \(f?\)

solutions.text:
If \(x\ge0\), then \(\lfloor|x|\rfloor=\lfloor x\rfloor=|\lfloor x\rfloor|\), so \(f(x)=0\).

If \(x\) is a negative integer, both terms equal \(|x|\), so again \(f(x)=0\).

If \(x\) is negative and not an integer, write \(x=-k-t\), where \(k\) is a nonnegative integer and \(0<t<1\). Then \(\lfloor|x|\rfloor=k\), while \(|\lfloor x\rfloor|=|-k-1|=k+1\), so \(f(x)=-1\).

Therefore, the range is \(\{-1,0\}.\)

Thus, the answer is A .
hints: Check positive numbers, integers, and negative non-integers separately
For negative non-integers, compare rounding before and after absolute value
